title: less
definition: A terminal pager program used to view the contents of a text file one screen at a time. It is the safe alternative to `cat` for reading large files.
simpleExplanation: Reading a book one page at a time. Instead of dumping all the text, it fills your screen, pauses, and lets you use the arrow keys to scroll down at your own pace.
realWorldExample: You need to read a massive server log. You type `less server.log`. You can easily scroll up and down, and even type `/error` to search the document for specific words.

basic: How do you exit the `less` program when you are done reading?
intermediate: Why does `less` load massive files so much faster than text editors like Vim or Nano?

answers.question: Why faster?
answers.answer: Because `less` does not read the entire file into RAM before starting. It only reads the tiny chunk of text needed to fill your current screen, making it open 100GB files instantly.
